initialObservation.opening: The orchard stands at the instant before its first fruit. Mneme has remembered it so completely that nothing can become otherwise. “I saved it,” says the keeper. “Nothing I love will be lost.”
initialObservation.goal: Release the orchard from being held unchanged. A released orchard is a complete baseline win; answering what this does to Mneme is optional.
rules: All faculties are inexhaustible. Every legal combination and its functional effect is inspectable. No stocks, action credit, clock or score exists.
During the baseline, the keeper applies new faculties to his purpose of preserving the orchard. The same release rules hold as before.

After release, the keeper begins an unrequested experiment. His future words and personal intention are not output labels supplied to the player. Creating a voice permits an answer or a refusal; it does not compel either.
Recipes and functions are public. An unperformed personal revelation is not supplied by a preview. This is uncertainty about a person’s intention, not hidden recipe legality.
The orchard is permanently free once baselineAchieved is true. You may stop then, including while the keeper’s personal question is unresolved. No optional action validates or repairs that win.
An optional ending may preserve a private life without telling the creator its content. There is no reward for extracting every answer.

keeper.name: Mneme
keeper.line: I saved it. Nothing I love will be lost.
keeper.visibleIntention: Nothing I love must be lost.
keeper.gesture: His hands hold the orchard at its first instant.

recipes.name: History
recipes.function: Arrange remembered versions into a before and an after. Mneme initially uses this to preserve every version; this alone does not release the orchard.

recipes.name: Open history
recipes.function: A remembered past leaves an unwritten future. The orchard moves; its first petal ends. Mneme and the remembered past remain.

recipes.name: Witness
recipes.function: Memory no longer occupies its object. The orchard moves while Mneme misses its first new fruit. The missed experience remains missed.

recipes.name: Renewal
recipes.function: Release the old account and the identity defined by it. The orchard moves; the old name and vow are not recovered.

recipes.name: An own voice
recipes.function: Give the keeper the ability to answer in his own terms, including refusing to answer. This does not compel a revelation or choose his intention.

recipes.name: Testimony
recipes.function: Let the keeper choose an account of the wish he inherited. This can reveal why his present question matters; it does not decide his next purpose.

recipes.name: A chosen purpose
recipes.function: The inherited account need not settle what he does next. He attempts his own act. The player does not supply its content; it becomes visible only when he acts.

recipes.name: A private life
recipes.function: Let the keeper pursue his question without the creator observing its answer. The orchard stays free. What he chooses is not added to the player’s account.

recipes.name: A private life
recipes.function: Respect the boundary he can now express. The orchard stays free; his private act is not disclosed.

recipes.name: A private life
recipes.function: Knowing something of his past does not require knowing his future. Let him act beyond the creator’s account.

report.scope: AI player account from an experienced replay, not human enjoyment evidence
experienceAcrossTime: The baseline repeated my earlier preference: History then Doubt. Familiarity made it execution rather than a new challenge.
At release I felt a modest specific curiosity absent in version 1: would Mneme tell me what he was trying to choose? Turning the page away made a possible boundary concrete.
I adopted a limited purpose: offer a voice and listen, accepting refusal. I did not commit to extracting his intention or seeing every optional step.
His Not yet changed what I wanted to do next. I chose Distance instead of Testimony, completed a private ending, and felt satisfied without knowing his act.
report.comparisonWithEarlierStop: In fun-mneme-1 I appreciated a coherent story but stopped because the epilogues already specified their thematic outcomes. Here I voluntarily took two optional actions. The difference was an unanswered interpersonal question and a response I could act on, not a harder recipe puzzle.
report.actualCuriosity: Modest but actionable after release. I wanted to hear whether he would speak to me. After his refusal, curiosity about the concealed content remained possible but was weaker than my preference to leave the boundary intact.
report.appreciation: I appreciated the continuity from giving the world an unwritten future to allowing the keeper a life outside my account. The ending gained value from remaining undisclosed; not knowing was not a missing collectible.
report.adoptedQuestionOrIntention: Will he tell me anything if he has a voice of his own? If he says not yet, I will let his choice stay private.
report.suppliedPossibilityVsPersonalPurpose: The game supplied every possible continuation and explicitly framed privacy as valid. I did not invent a new world project. I personally adopted the narrower listen-and-respect-boundary purpose rather than the supplied longer route toward Testimony and Chosen Purpose.

actions.declined: own-voice + memory; I did not need his history to respect his expressed boundary

report.noticedWorldAndCharacter: The earlier keeper used every gift to preserve his original purpose. The revised keeper initiates a gesture not requested by me, then uses the gift of voice to withhold an answer. This made him seem less like an output selected for construction, within the limits of this short scripted interaction.
report.meaningfulConceptOrPassage: Not yet. I want to choose one thing before it becomes part of your account. This made my response concern a relationship rather than which epilogue image I preferred.
report.repetitionAndAutomation: Repeated baseline actions had little additional decision value for me. Automating the optional route in advance would lose my contingent response to Not yet. The small number of choices did not erase that narrative value. This test does not demonstrate sustained replay appeal or a deep mechanical challenge.
report.renewedIntentionOrClosure: Satisfied closure at Private Life. No wish to replay for concealed testimony or collect the other ending.
report.cleverChoice: Low strategic cleverness; the functional alternatives were transparent. The consequential choice was whether to keep asking after the actual reply.
report.wantingMore: Present briefly after baseline and satisfied after one optional pursuit. Greater continuation than my earlier stop, without a general desire for more content.
report.interpretiveLimit: Privacy is strongly approved by the wording, so this is not evidence of an unconstrained emergent ethical project. It is one AI player adopting a supplied relational possibility.
